exposure: Mother-infant dyads were grouped by: vaginally delivered infants without antibiotics, vaginally delivered infants exposed to antibiotics, and infants born by caesarean section with routine maternal prophylactic antibiotics.
cohort: Twenty-five mother-infant dyads were selected from the longitudinal Queensland Family Cohort Study.
finding: For infants, delivery mode appears to have a larger effect on gut microbiome composition at 6 weeks post-partum than intrapartum antibiotic exposure.
mod_finding: Caesarean section infants exhibited decreases in Bacteroidetes, changes to several functional pathways and altered beta diversity, while minimal differences due to antibiotic exposure were detected.
